rule_findings.title: Successful login after repeated failures
rule_findings.description: 6 failed logins from 10.0.5.23 were followed by a successful login for admin within 10 minutes.

rule_findings.title: Successful login at unusual hour
rule_findings.description: admin logged in from 10.0.5.23 at 02:14. Review indicator, not proof of compromise.

rule_findings.title: Sudo activity after suspicious login
rule_findings.description: admin ran sudo (/usr/bin/cat /etc/shadow) shortly after a suspicious login. This shows sudo use, not confirmed privilege escalation.

summary: The system experienced a brute force attack followed by a successful login, with subsequent sudo activity.

attack_chain.explanation: The brute force attack was detected by the 'ssh_brute_force' rule.
The 'failure_then_success' rule identified a successful login after the brute force attack.
The 'login_then_sudo' rule detected sudo activity after the successful login.

mitigations: Implement rate limiting on SSH login attempts to prevent brute force attacks.
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all administrative accounts.
Restrict sudo access to specific commands and users to prevent privilege escalation.
Regularly review sudo logs for unusual activity.
Configure SSH to use public key authentication only, disabling password authentication.
